The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```java
assertEquals("PLAIN auth failed: wrong password", e.getMessage());
```
Reason:
The test case `testSaslPlainServerBadPassword` was expecting an exact match of the error message when authentication failed. This strict comparison caused the test to fail if the actual error message varied even slightly, indicating a lack of robustness in handling different error message formats.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```java
String message = e.getMessage();
assertContains("PLAIN auth failed", message);
assertContains("wrong password", message);
```
Reason:
The fix introduces a more flexible approach by checking if the error message contains specific substrings rather than requiring an exact match. This allows the test to pass even if the actual error message varies slightly, thus making the test more robust against different error message formats.
